title: Free well-being test (WHO-5 Well-Being Index): score 0–100 — cv.cm
description: Free WHO-5 well-being test online. Answer 5 questions about the last two weeks to get your well-being score from 0 to 100 and what it means. Private: nothing leaves your browser.
lede: The WHO-5 Well-Being Index asks 5 short questions about how you have felt over the last two weeks. It takes under a minute and gives a score from 0 to 100.
about: The WHO-5 was published by the World Health Organization Regional Office for Europe in 1998 and is one of the most widely used well-being questionnaires in the world. It is free to use. Each answer scores 0 to 5; the total (0–25) is multiplied by 4 to give a percentage from 0 (worst possible) to 100 (best possible).
A score below 52 suggests poor well-being, and doctors use it as a reason to check for depression; a score of 28 or less often goes with depression. This test is a self-check, not a diagnosis.

faq.q: What does my WHO-5 score mean?
faq.a: Multiply the raw score (0–25) by 4. 52 or more is in the normal range of well-being. Below 52 suggests poor well-being. 28 or less is a sign that depression may be present and should be checked by a professional.

faq.q: Is the WHO-5 a depression test?
faq.a: It measures positive well-being, not depression symptoms, but a low score is a good reason to screen for depression, for example with the PHQ-9 test on this site, and to talk to a doctor.

faq.q: How often can I take it?
faq.a: It asks about the last two weeks, so retaking it every two weeks or so is a simple way to track how you're doing. A change of 10 points or more is considered meaningful.
Regular sleep, daylight and movement, time with people you like, and doing things that interest you help many people. If a low mood lasts, talk to a doctor or counselor.

items: I have felt cheerful and in good spirits.
I have felt calm and relaxed.
I have felt active and vigorous.
I woke up feeling fresh and rested.
My daily life has been filled with things that interest me.

low.name: Low well-being (0–28)
low.body: Your answers suggest your well-being has been low over the last two weeks. Scores this low often go with depression, so please talk to a doctor or mental health professional soon. You can also take the PHQ-9 depression check here. You don't have to handle this alone, and effective help exists.

reduced.name: Reduced well-being (32–48)
reduced.body: Your well-being has been below the usual range lately. It's worth checking for depression (the PHQ-9 test on this site is one way) and talking to a doctor if this has gone on for a while. Small steps like regular sleep, daylight, movement and time with people you trust can help.

good.name: Good well-being (52–100)
good.body: Your well-being is in the normal range. Keep up the habits and people that help you feel this way, and retake the check in a few weeks to see how it holds up.
